Issue:
For as long as I can remember, not just a year ago when I asked for help, whenever I would use the internet for... anything, I would watch my DL speed change from every tick to
450KB/s - 10KB/s - 350KB/s - 0KB/s - 250KB/s - 40B/s - 370 KB/s - 350KB/s - 0KB/s - SrslyFkingStopKB/s
And the craziest part about it was that it ONLY HAPPENS ON MY COMPUTER, regardless of whether it is using WiFi or an Ethernet cable - which makes the solution make even less sense.

Fruitless Attempts:
Changing my WiFi password to ATTSucks after calling them out for the fourth time didn't seem to help, even if it got a laugh out of the techs the fifth and sixth time.
Updating/rollback/reinstall drivers, full reset of Windows, full whipe and then reinstallation of Windows, new ethernet cable, WiFi booster, none of them helped.

Final Solution:
Device Manager > Network Adapters > Realtek PCIe GbE Family Controller > Advanced:

*ARP Offload: Disabled
*Flow Control: Disabled
*Interrupt Moderation: Disabled
*IPv4 Checksum Offload: Rx & Tx Enabled

*Large Send Offload v2(IPv4): Disabled
*Large Send Offload v2(IPv6): Disabled
*NS Offload: Disabled
If I change any one of these back to its orginal setting, my internet goes right back to jumping around again, which, I may not be a professional in this kind of stuff, but it makes absolutely no sense to me at all how these all can have the exact same effect.
I get that they're all essentially (extra) buffers, but I would assume the IPv4 setting couldn't effect IPv6 and vice versa, which, changing one either of them or both has the same effect on my computer.
If someone smarter than me about this stuff wants to point out how TF these settings being turned on could possibly punch my internet in the face every other tick, that would be great.

Something like a year ago, I was asking for help with my internet, as it would go full speed then drop to 0 repeatedly every tick - I finally fixed it.
